explication:
<explanation>
1. Project type & purpose  
   • This is a pure CLI application (“GoReleaser”) whose job is “release engineering, simplified.”  
   • It reads a YAML config, orchestrates a sequence of “pipes” (build, archive, sign, publish, etc.), interacts with VCS hosts (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea) and package registries, and emits artifacts to the filesystem and remote repositories.

2. High‐level folder structure & mapping to system components  
   • cmd/ – CLI interface layer (each Go file under cmd/ is a Cobra‐style subcommand: build, check, release, publish, announce, etc.)  
   • main.go – boots the app, wires together config, context, commands  
   • pkg/ – reusable libraries: config loader (pkg/config), context builder (pkg/context), defaults, healthcheck, archive utilities (pkg/archive)  
   • internal/ – core engine:  
     – pipeline orchestration (internal/pipeline, internal/pipe/*)  
     – each “pipe” plugin (archive, build, publish, sign, upload, changelog, checksums, etc.)  
     – builders for supported languages (internal/builders/{go, rust, zig,…})  
     – clients for external services (internal/client/{github, gitlab, gitea,…})  
     – filesystem & artifact I/O (internal/archivefiles, internal/artifact, internal/gio)  
     – error handling & middleware (internal/gerrors, internal/middleware)  
   • www/ – static site generator and docs (not part of runtime)  
   • scripts/ – build, test, documentation helper scripts  
   • testdata/ & _test.go throughout for unit/integration tests

3. Core components & interactions  
   [CLI ENTRYPOINT]  
     main.go → parses flags, loads pkg/config ← config.yaml (internal/static)  
     ↓  
     cmd/*.Go (Build, Check, Release, etc.) invoke →  
     ↓  
   [PIPELINE ORCHESTRATOR] (internal/pipeline)  
     • Receives a context (pkg/context + defaults) and a list of enabled pipes  
     • Iterates over internal/pipe/<name> modules in configured order  
     • Each pipe module implements a standard interface: Run(context) → error  
     ↓  
   [PIPE EXECUTION]  
     • File operations: internal/archivefiles, internal/artifact, pkg/archive produce tar/zips  
     • Language builds: internal/builders/* compile targets  
     • Clients: internal/client/* create releases, fetch diffs, post comments  
     • Signers: internal/sign orchestrate Docker/cosign/GPG signing  
     • Uploaders: internal/pipe/upload, internal/pipe/docker push images  
     • Changelog, checksums, metadata pipes read/write files, generate docs  
     ↓  
   [OUTPUT & EXTERNAL]  
     • Writes artifacts to local filesystem (artifacts/…)  
     • Calls external APIs (GitHub/GitLab/Gitea, Docker Registry, Homebrew, AUR, etc.)

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   • Command pattern – each subcommand in cmd/ maps to a user‐visible action  
   • Pipeline pattern – decoupled, sequential “pipes” implementing a common interface  
   • Plugin‐like modularity – new pipes or builders can be added under internal/pipe or internal/builders  
   • Dependency injection via context object – carries config, logger, temp dirs, etc.  

5. Diagramming guidelines (tailored for a CLI tool)  
   a. Show folder‐module mapping: group components by folder (cmd, pkg, internal)  
   b. Use rectangles for modules, cylinders for local storage (filesystem), clouds for external services  
   c. Color code:  
     – Blue: CLI & config (main.go, cmd/, pkg/config, internal/static)  
     – Green: Pipeline core (internal/pipeline, internal/pipe/*)  
     – Orange: Builders & file I/O (internal/builders, internal/archivefiles, pkg/archive)  
     – Purple: External clients (internal/client, internal/pipe/* that call APIs)  
   d. Draw directional arrows:  
     – User → CLI Entrypoint  
     – CLI → Config Loader → Context Builder  
     – CLI → Pipeline Orchestrator → Pipe Modules (in sequence)  
     – Pipes → File I/O (filesystem cylinder)  
     – Pipes → External Services (cloud icons for GitHub, Docker Hub, Homebrew, etc.)  
   e. Annotate each arrow with the data in motion (e.g., “config struct,” “artifact files,” “API calls”)

6. Including features & folder structure  
   • Overlay the list of main features (build, archive, sign, publish, announce, check, healthcheck) next to their implementing packages under internal/pipe and cmd/  
   • Show internal/builders/* modules branching off from the “build” pipe  
   • Show internal/client modules feeding into the “announce” and “publish” pipes  
   • Indicate pkg/config reading internal/static/config.yaml and feeding all components  

7. Final checklist  
   – Clear labels on modules (folder paths + responsibility)  
   – Arrows with direction and brief payload descriptions  
   – Color coding / shapes to distinguish CLI, core engine, file I/O, external  
   – Folder‐to‐feature mapping so someone reading the diagram sees “cmd/release.go → ’release’ command → internal/pipe/release”  

By following this layout, you’ll produce a detailed system design diagram that captures GoReleaser’s architecture, aligns modules with their folders, and highlights the flow from user invocation through pipelines to artifact generation and external interactions.  
</explanation>
